assessment.necessity_reason: The dump API supports a finite constructed JSON value deeper than JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, and do_dump now fails when traversal reaches that depth. The old harness dumps only values returned by json_loadb. Parsing rejects values beyond the limit; with parsing starting at depth 1 and dumping at depth 0, a successfully parsed value cannot reach the dump guard. Neither dump mode constructs a deeper value.

before.requirement: Reach a clean do_dump failure when traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
before.reason: The complete old do_dump body has no depth limit rejection.

after.requirement: Reach the supported do_dump failure for a JSON value whose traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
after.reason: The new guard returns failure at the limit. The API test supplies an array beyond the limit, but the harness sends only successfully parsed values to dumping. parse_value rejects values beyond the limit, while dump traversal begins one depth level lower than parsing. The harness has no other route to a deeper value.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Array dumping recursively increases traversal depth.
The API test supplies nested arrays beyond the limit and checks that dumping fails.
json_loadb returns the value produced by parse_json.
Parsing starts at depth zero and delegates value construction to parse_value.
parse_value increments depth and rejects values beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
Callback dumping invokes do_dump at depth zero; string dumping delegates to callback dumping.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same depth limit tuple is absent from old do_dump and supported by new do_dump. The old harness cannot reach the new behavior because its only dumped objects come from the depth limited parser.
